title: 2-week React skill test plan
summary: Prepare for a timed React skill test: 17 lessons, 20 runnable TSX exercises checked in the browser, a React flashcard deck and two runs of the timed simulator. About 1–1.5 hours a day.

rhythm.text: Read one or two lessons, try every gotcha before opening its answer, then make the exercises pass without looking at the hints first.
Timed practice or a full test, then review: reread the lessons for weak topics and clear due flashcards.

rules: Predict what a snippet renders or logs before you check the answer.
Never mutate state or props: copy, then change the copy.
Every effect that subscribes, times or fetches needs a cleanup.
Query the DOM the way a user would: by role, label and text.
Keep the timer honest in practice runs: no notes and no pausing.

typescript: Type props with an interface or type alias and destructure them in the parameter list.
Give useState an explicit type when it starts empty: useState<User | null>(null).
Use React.ReactNode for children and React.ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement> for input handlers.
Type reducer actions as a discriminated union so each case narrows its payload.
Make reusable lists generic: function List<T>({ items, render }: Props<T>).

phases.title: Core React
phases.check: Without notes, build a filtered, sorted list with a controlled search box and an effect with cleanup, and explain why each key, dependency and copy is needed.

phases.title: Advanced React and the test
phases.check: Score 70% or more in every topic of the timed simulator, and pass both coding tasks within the time limit.

weeks.title: Rendering, state, events, forms and effects
weeks.focus: How React renders, why state is a snapshot, immutable updates, keys, controlled inputs and effects with cleanup. Finish with a timed practice run.

tip.typescript: Type every component's props, and let TypeScript infer state when the initial value is not empty.
